title: Masked-autoencoder fusion for ASD classification with incomplete multimodal data
summary: The MMR-MF3 framework combines fMRI connectivity and behavioral features using modality-specific encoders, masked-autoencoder imputation, cross-modal transformer fusion and sex-stratified classification heads. On ABIDE I/II data, the paper reports AUC 0.89 for males and 0.86 for females and evaluates generalization with leave-one-site-out cross-validation. This is retrospective dataset evaluation; it does not establish diagnostic benefit or clinical deployment.
ai_technology: A masked autoencoder reconstructs missing modalities and a cross-modal transformer fuses fMRI connectivity and behavioral features for sex-stratified ASD classification.
organization: Metropolitan University; Islamic University of Technology; University of California, Irvine

evidence.tested: Retrospective ABIDE I/II datasets; fivefold and leave-one-site-out validation, modality-missingness experiments, ablations and SHAP analysis.
evidence.unknown: No prospective clinical evaluation or clinical benefit was established; ABIDE retrospective validation does not establish real-world diagnostic utility.
